question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $5$ and $12$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $5\cdot 12=60.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,5)\,⟹\,x=2+5t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 2+5t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $12$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $5\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,12).$ So, we multiply both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5\cdot 5t & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ t & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=5+12s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2+5t \\  & =2+5(5+12s) \\  & =27+60s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡27\,(\text{mod}\,60)$ is the unique solution modulo $60,$ and $x=27$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
